questions.question: What is a Class 1 hazardous material?

options.text: An explosive
Radioactive material
Corrosive material

questions.correctAnswerText: An explosive
questions.explanation: Class 1 hazardous materials are explosives. These include ammunition, dynamite, and fireworks.

questions.question: During the basic control skills test, can you exit your vehicle to check its position?

options.text: No, you cannot stop and exit the vehicle.
You are encouraged not to exit the vehicle.
Yes, only if the vehicle is in reverse.
Yes, only if the vehicle is in neutral with the parking brake set.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, only if the vehicle is in neutral with the parking brake set.
questions.explanation: During the basic control skills test, you may exit your vehicle only if it is in neutral and the parking brake is set. You may check the vehicle's position up to two times, except during straight line backing, when you may look only once.

questions.question: What might rust around wheel nuts mean?

options.text: It rained recently
The nuts are loose
The nuts are too tight

questions.correctAnswerText: The nuts are loose
questions.explanation: Before every drive, inspect your tires. Rust around wheel nuts may show that the nuts are loose.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT an example of a hazardous driver?

options.text: A driver operating a vehicle without scraping ice off the windshield
The operator of a rental truck
The driver of a station wagon with items covering the back windows
A person operating a pick-up truck

questions.correctAnswerText: A person operating a pick-up truck
questions.explanation: Drivers with blocked vision are hazards on the road. Examples include drivers with ice on their windshield, drivers in vehicles with items blocking windows, and drivers of rental trucks who are not used to limited rear visibility. Simply driving a pick-up truck is not hazardous.

questions.question: In cold temperatures, when do bridges usually freeze?

options.text: After other parts of the road
Before other parts of the road
At the same time as other parts of the road

questions.correctAnswerText: Before other parts of the road
questions.explanation: Bridges freeze before other road surfaces in cold weather. When driving in cold, wet conditions, be extra careful on bridges and overpasses.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you must be able to do everything about oil EXCEPT:

options.text: Indicate where the dipstick is located
Show that the oil level is in a safe range
Show that the oil level is above the refill mark
Show that the oil level is below the refill mark

questions.correctAnswerText: Show that the oil level is below the refill mark
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you must locate the dipstick, show the oil level is safe, and show the oil is above the refill mark. You should NOT show oil below the refill mark.

questions.question: In heavy traffic, what is the safest driving speed?

options.text: The posted speed limit
The speed of surrounding traffic
Much slower than surrounding traffic

questions.correctAnswerText: The speed of surrounding traffic
questions.explanation: In heavy traffic, match the speed of surrounding vehicles. Vehicles moving the same direction at the same speed are unlikely to collide. However, do not exceed the speed limit.

questions.question: Why should charter bus passengers wait until departure time to board?

options.text: The bus cost starts when the first passenger boards, so late boarding saves money
Passengers will get on and off multiple times and may miss the departure
Passengers cannot choose their seats until the bus is about to leave
Waiting to load helps prevent theft and vandalism

questions.correctAnswerText: Waiting to load helps prevent theft and vandalism
questions.explanation: Charter bus drivers should not let passengers board until departure time. This helps prevent theft and vandalism.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing without warning lights or gates, what should you do?

options.text: Do not worry because the tracks are likely abandoned
Park your vehicle and walk to the tracks to check for trains
Look down the tracks in both directions to check for approaching trains
Do what other vehicles are doing

questions.correctAnswerText: Look down the tracks in both directions to check for approaching trains
questions.explanation: At a passive railroad crossing (no gates or lights), you must look both directions on the tracks before crossing to make sure no trains are coming.

questions.question: After starting the engine, how long does oil pressure take to reach a normal level?

options.text: Within a few seconds
About one minute
About four minutes
Within 10 minutes of driving

questions.correctAnswerText: Within a few seconds
questions.explanation: After you start the engine, watch the gauges. Oil pressure should reach a normal level within a few seconds.

questions.question: When checking the engine compartment, what should you do?

options.text: Do not engage the parking brake.
Block the wheels.
Keep the engine running.
Put the gearshift in first gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Block the wheels.
questions.explanation: Before you check the engine compartment, set the parking brake and block the wheels. Check the engine before you get in the cab and start the engine.

questions.question: When backing up, you should:

options.text: Move quickly to get out of other drivers' way.
Try not to use your mirrors.
Back from any position.
Use a helper if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use a helper if possible.
questions.explanation: Backing up a large vehicle is always dangerous because you cannot see everything behind you. If you need to back up, use a helper when you can.

questions.question: Before you drive a bus that has been parked for several days, what should you do?

options.text: Assume the interior is in good working order.
Call the local police department.
Walk through the bus to check for any damage since the last trip.
Ask passengers to check the interior of the bus.

questions.correctAnswerText: Walk through the bus to check for any damage since the last trip.
questions.explanation: People sometimes damage buses that are parked. Before you drive a bus that has been sitting unused, always check the inside to make sure everything is safe for passengers.

questions.question: To leave a stop safely, you should park so that:

options.text: You must back up to leave your parking space.
You can pull forward to leave your parking space.
You park on the side of the road, not in a parking lot.
You back into the parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pull forward to leave your parking space.
questions.explanation: Backing up is dangerous, so avoid it when you can. Park so you can pull forward and exit your parking space.

questions.question: When you turn quickly to avoid an object in the road, you should:

options.text: Apply your brakes as you steer.
Turn more than you need to give yourself extra clearance.
Turn only as much as needed to miss the object.
Steer and accelerate at the same time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only as much as needed to miss the object.
questions.explanation: When you turn quickly to avoid an object, turn only enough to clear it. Do not brake while turning.

questions.question: Hazardous materials must be marked with all of the following, except:

options.text: The material's name.
The material's identification number.
The correct hazard label.
The phone number of a contact person.

questions.correctAnswerText: The phone number of a contact person.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials must show the material's name, identification number, and hazard label. Do not transport hazardous materials unless you are sure it is allowed.

questions.question: If your wheels start to spin when you accelerate on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Use the brakes.
Release the accelerator.
Keep accelerating.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the accelerator.
questions.explanation: If your drive wheels start to spin while you accelerate on a slippery surface, take your foot off the accelerator.

questions.question: While driving, you should:

options.text: Think ahead about how to handle dangerous situations.
Enjoy the scenery.
Never use your mirrors.
Focus only on your own driving and ignore other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Think ahead about how to handle dangerous situations.
questions.explanation: While driving, always watch the road ahead for hazards. Plan how you would handle any danger that could happen.

questions.question: Loose belts in the engine compartment will:

options.text: Not spin the water pump or fan properly, which causes the engine to overheat.
Make the engine run more efficiently.
Make the fan run too much, causing the engine to run too cold.
Last longer than tight belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not spin the water pump or fan properly, which causes the engine to overheat.
questions.explanation: Check that all belts in the engine compartment are tight. Loose belts do not spin the water pump or fan properly, which can cause the engine to overheat.

questions.question: When driving long distances, you should:

options.text: Take rest breaks.
Drive as fast as possible.
Drive through the night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take rest breaks.
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue on a long trip, take a break every 100 miles or every two hours. Driving at night or when you would normally sleep increases the risk of fatigue.
